# `screen`

A screen of the interface: its variables, its layout tree and its keys (12 §10.1).

## Fields

Besides these, a definition takes the [keys every definition carries](README.md#keys-every-definition-carries).

- `title` ([`Prop`](#prop), or `null`; optional): The screen's title.
- `context` (string, or `null`; optional): The keymap context (12 §9.2) the screen's keys are named in. Left out, `menu`. `debug` also lets the screen see truth and use the development widgets.
- `params` (object, name → string; optional): The values the screen is opened with: each name and its type, such as `"who": "entity"`. Read by bindings as `$name`.
- `vars` (object, name → [`Literal`](#literal); optional): The screen's own variables and their starting values. Read by bindings as `screen.name`; written by widgets and the `set` effect.
- `min_size` (list of 2: whole number, 0 or more, whole number, 0 or more, or `null`; optional): The smallest grid the screen can be shown on, as `[columns, rows]`. On a smaller one the screen is replaced by a notice saying how large the window must be.
- `layout` (object; **required**): The layout tree.
- `keys` (object, name → list of object; optional): What the screen does when a key with one of these names (12 §9.2) is pressed and no widget used it: each a list of effects.
- `popup` (object [`PopupDef`](#popupdef), or `null`; optional): `popup`: the screen does not fill the frame. It is drawn over the screens beneath it, which stay on show.

<a id="prop"></a>
### `Prop`

A widget property that is either written outright or computed.

A `Bound` property holds its `Binding`: the source of an expression or a text template and, once the screen's definition has been compiled, the compiled form. A screen shows a placeholder for one that was never compiled or never evaluated.

Takes (kept with where it was written, and checked when mods load):

- a string

<a id="literal"></a>
### `Literal`

A literal value in a definition: `true`, `3`, `0.5` or `"text"`.

Written as true, false, a number or a text.

Takes:

- a string
- an integer
- a number
- a boolean

<a id="popupdef"></a>
### `PopupDef`

`popup`: the size and place of a screen that does not fill the frame (12 §10.1).

- `width` ([`Size`](#size), or `null`; optional): The popup's width: cells, a percentage of the frame, or `"fit"`. Left out, it fits its content.
- `height` ([`Size`](#size), or `null`; optional): The popup's height, likewise.
- `place` ([`Place`](#place); optional): Where it sits in the frame. Left out, in the middle.
- `dim` (`true` or `false`; optional): Whether everything beneath it is drawn dimmed.

<a id="size"></a>
### `Size`

How large a node is along one axis.

Written as a size: a number of cells, `"50%"`, `"fit"`, `"fill"` or `{ "fill": weight }`.

Takes:

- a string
- an object: object, name → any JSON value
- an integer

<a id="place"></a>
### `Place`

Where a popup sits in the frame.

One of:

- `"center"`: In the middle.
- `"centre"`: In the middle.
- `"top"`: Against the top edge, in the middle of it.
- `"bottom"`: Against the bottom edge.
- `"left"`: Against the left edge.
- `"right"`: Against the right edge.
- `"top_left"`: In the top left corner.
- `"top_right"`: In the top right corner.
- `"bottom_left"`: In the bottom left corner.
- `"bottom_right"`: In the bottom right corner.
